headline: Deliberate practice is focused improvement—working on weaknesses with feedback, not just repetition
universal_truth: Improvement requires intention; doing something repeatedly doesn't mean doing it better
fun_facts: Expert performers in most fields have accumulated about 10,000 hours of deliberate practice
Deliberate practice feels effortful—if it's comfortable, you're not in the learning zone
Feedback within seconds leads to 3x faster improvement than delayed feedback
discussion_questions: When do you practice deliberately versus just go through motions?
What skill would improve most from focused, intentional work?
How do you get feedback on your weaknesses?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Playing guitar for 20 years doesn't make you a master—practicing deliberately does. Deliberate practice targets weaknesses, seeks feedback, and pushes past comfort. Repetition without intention is just motion.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We often confuse activity with improvement. What's the difference between practice and deliberate practice?

options.text: Deliberate practice targets specific weaknesses with immediate feedback—it's uncomfortable because you're working at the edge of your ability, not reinforcing what you already know
options.response: Yes. Comfort means you're not learning. Deliberate practice is effortful, focused, and targeted at weaknesses. That's what builds skill. Easy practice just maintains.

options.text: More practice hours lead to more skill
options.response: Hours matter, but quality matters more—10 focused hours beat 100 unfocused ones...

q1.title: Comfort Zone vs Learning Zone
q1.script: In the comfort zone, you're not learning—just reinforcing. In the learning zone, you're slightly beyond current ability. That's where growth happens. Deliberate practice keeps you in the learning zone.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Comfort Zone vs Learning Zone"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Feedback Loop
q2.script: Without feedback, you can't correct. Deliberate practice includes immediate feedback so errors become adjustments. The faster the feedback, the faster the improvement.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Target Weaknesses
q3.script: It's fun to practice what you're good at. Deliberate practice targets what you're bad at. That's uncomfortable but effective. Skill gaps don't close without focused attention.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Improvement requires intention. Doing something repeatedly doesn't mean doing it better. Practice deliberately.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 285. Tomorrow, we'll explore when practice becomes skill—mastery. Until then, identify where you could practice more deliberately.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Deliberate Practice Plan - What Needs Focused Work?
growTrack.learning_objective: Design deliberate practice for skill improvement
growTrack.activity: Choose a skill you want to improve. What specifically is weak? How can you get immediate feedback? Design a 30-minute deliberate practice session targeting your specific weaknesses.
